name: Turkey Tater Tot Hotdish
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Midwest hotdish, the single most batch-friendly casserole shape there is. Source is a macro-tracked recipe: 378 cal / 27.3g protein at 5 servings, so scaling turkey up to a 14-serving pan puts us comfortably over 500 cal with 35g+ protein. | HARVEST:
OVERRIDE Tater Tots: splitter split '5 servings ... 420 grams' - source states 420 g
intro_html: In Minnesota and the Dakotas this is not a casserole, it is a hotdish, and correcting people on that is practically a regional sport. Seasoned ground turkey and a creamy mushroom base underneath, a full armor of tater tots on top, baked until the tots go golden and crackly. Each serving runs 563 calories with 28 grams of protein for about $1.79. It is the friendliest dish in this whole collection to make on a Sunday and eat all week.
ingredients_display: Cream of Mushroom Soup (Campbell's (USDA SR)): 3 cans (876 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Cream of Mushroom Soup, 3 cans: ~$2.18. Buy 3 10.5oz cans: $2.22.
Pantry seasonings (salt, black pepper, smoked paprika): ~$0.59. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $25.11 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.79 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $27.36 across 14 servings, roughly $1.95 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $15.03 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $42.39. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $1.79 a serving, and most of that is the turkey. Tater tots, canned soup, and shredded cheddar are three of the steadiest low-price items in the freezer and center aisles, which is exactly why this dish has fed the upper Midwest for sixty years.
shop_smart: The single large bag of tater tots beats buying several small ones almost every time. Check the per-ounce tag, then buy the big bag and keep what you do not use frozen for the next batch.
Cream of mushroom soup is the base and you need three cans. Store-brand condensed soup performs the same in a bake, since it is getting stirred into meat and covered in cheese either way.
Buy the block-free route on cheese only if it is cheaper. Pre-shredded 8 oz bags are usually the better deal on cheddar, and a hotdish does not care about the anti-caking starch.
Ground turkey is the whole cost story here. Watch for it to hit a sale price and buy several packs, because it freezes for months without losing anything.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high and brown the ground turkey, breaking it into small crumbles as it cooks.
Add the diced onion and the garlic, cook 5 minutes until the onion turns soft and translucent, then season with salt, black pepper, and smoked paprika.
Turn off the heat and stir in all three cans of condensed cream of mushroom soup along with about half the shredded cheddar. Do not thin it with water; the tots release moisture as they bake.
Spread the turkey mixture into a greased 9x13 pan and press it flat so the tot layer sits level.
Arrange the tater tots over the top in tight rows, edge to edge. A packed layer bakes into a crust; a scattered one just steams.
Bake at 400F for 40 to 45 minutes, until the tots are deep golden and the edges of the pan are bubbling.
Scatter the rest of the cheddar over the tots, return the pan for 5 minutes to melt it, then rest 10 minutes before portioning.
portion_html: Put the pan on the scale, subtract the empty pan weight, and divide by 14. Cut squares to that weight rather than eyeballing them, because the corners always look bigger than they are. Every serving comes to 563 calories and 28 grams of protein.
credit_html: Recipe adapted from ohsnapmacros.com, rebuilt for 14-serving budget meal prep with weighed portions and Omaha pricing.
upsell_html: A whole week of hotdish for about $1.79 a serving. This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

head.description: Turkey tater tot hotdish meal prep: ground turkey in a creamy mushroom base under a crisp tot crust. 563 calories, 28g protein, about $1.79 a serving.
head.keywords: turkey tater tot hotdish, tater tot casserole, ground turkey casserole, midwest hotdish, budget meal prep, 9x13 casserole, cheap dinner
steps: Brown the ground turkey in olive oil, then cook the onion and garlic in with it and season with salt, pepper, and smoked paprika.
Off the heat, stir in the condensed cream of mushroom soup and half the shredded cheddar.
Spread the mixture into a greased 9x13 pan and press it level.
Cover the top edge to edge with tater tots and bake at 400F for 40 to 45 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Top with the remaining cheddar, melt 5 minutes, rest 10 minutes, then portion into 14 containers.
